current_text.html: Although references are sometimes proper, in general it is better that every court should discharge the duty assigned it under the law of the Church. A higher court is not required to accede to the request of the lower, but it should ordinarily give advice when so requested.

relationships.title: Presbytery standing rule exempting retired ministers from reporting

occurrences.excerpt: Illiana Presbytery's proposed rule relieving retired ministers from mandatory reporting was found not in conflict with BCO 23-2, with the presbytery advised to use its own wisdom under BCO 41-5.

relationships.title: Request by a Presbytery for CCB Review of a Document Specifying Acceptable and Unacceptable Exceptions

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB declined a non-judicial reference asking it to review a presbytery's list of acceptable and unacceptable ordination exceptions, citing the complexity of issues better resolved through judicial processes.

relationships.title: Interpretation of 'papists' in WCF 24.3 for marriage eligibility

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB declined Iowa Presbytery's reference asking whether 'papists' in WCF 24.3 means all Roman Catholics or only those holding Roman Catholic soteriology, finding no matter pending before the lower court.

relationships.title: Declaring exceptions for non-literal six-day creationist views
relationships.disposition: declined to take action — reference not proper; overture recommended for proper procedure

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB declined to act, ruling that defining what constitutes an exception to the standards is beyond its scope; presbyteries wishing to set such a norm should overture the GA.

relationships.title: Setting a nomination deadline before the one-month officer election notice
relationships.disposition: advice given — session may set nomination deadline before one-month meeting notice; all six required elements must be included

occurrences.excerpt: A session may set a nomination deadline before the one-month congregational meeting notice expires, but all six BCO 24-1 requirements for officer election must be met.

relationships.title: Effect of GA refusal to accept a judicial reference on lower-court proceedings

occurrences.excerpt: The committee's recommendation and the Assembly's determination refusing a judicial reference apply to the entire judicial process in PCA courts, clarifying that no parties were left without recourse.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained an appeal by seven members of a 38-member mission church who were convicted by their temporary Session of opposing the organizing minister's expected election as pastor. Reversing the Presbytery's affirmance and the guilty verdicts underlying indefinite suspensions, the SJC held the indictments fatally lacked BCO 32-5 specificity; Presbytery used the wrong standard of review; the Session had no authority to control pastoral selection; and no Fifth or Ninth Commandment offense was proved. Challenges to witness-judges, venue, and refusal to refer were rejected.

metadata.synopsis: Blue Ridge Presbytery requested that the Standing Judicial Commission hear and decide a complaint because of claimed bias and constitutional questions. The SJC denied the request for reference, holding that the record did not demonstrate affirmative bias, serious division, constitutional questions, or delicate issues that would warrant reference under BCO 41-2. The presbytery was directed to hear and decide the complaint itself.

metadata.synopsis: Teaching and ruling elders challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Gregory Lawrence’s acquittal on five doctrinal charges. The SJC sustained the complaint on procedural grounds: the trial commission relied on his post-indictment exculpatory writings while he declined to testify, depriving the prosecution of cross-examination. The SJC ordered a new trial on the same indictment under specified evidentiary procedures. Because this was a complaint rather than an appeal, it did not reverse the acquittals into findings of guilt or decide the doctrinal merits.

topics: peace and purity of the church
metadata.synopsis: Members challenged Presbytery’s denial of their complaint against a Session instruction not to circulate an open letter repeating allegations against their pastor. The SJC denied the complaint, leaving the instruction in force. It held that liberty of conscience does not eliminate members’ obligation to obey lawful church injunctions. Here the members had sought the Session’s advice, Presbytery had found no strong presumption of chargeable offenses, and renewed circulation would disturb the church’s peace; under those circumstances, the Session acted within its authority.

metadata.synopsis: Central Carolina Presbytery asked the SJC to adjudicate two complaints and a related reference concerning charges against church members. Although initially found administratively in order, the reference was declined because adjudicating only the formally referred matters could render at least two additional, related complaints moot without due consideration. All matters in Case 92-8 were returned to Presbytery; no underlying merits were decided.
